What to do during an Allstate outage, from calling your agent and documenting damage to protecting proof of insurance and avoiding scams that target policyholders.

It has been revealed that A local Allstate $ALL agent is a human contact who can answer coverage questions, help start a claim and pass details to the company while the app or website is unavailable. Agent contact details usually appear on policy paperwork. That means the office can be reached without logging in to anything.

It has been revealed that the declarations page is usually the first place to look. This is the summary sheet that lists a policy's coverages, limits and deductibles, and it often names the servicing agent. Renewal notices, billing statements and welcome letters can carry the same name, phone number and office address.

Recent findings suggest that older emails, text messages and voicemails from the agency are another record worth checking. A policyholder who saved the agent's number in a phone's contacts already has the quickest route. If an office number turns up through an online search instead, compare it with the printed paperwork before calling.

Policyholders are generally expected to take reasonable steps to stop damage from getting worse, even when they cannot reach their insurer. An app or website being down does not pause that duty. Make temporary fixes, keep every receipt and hold off on permanent repairs until an adjuster has seen the loss.

Sources indicate that standard homeowners policy language spells this out. The common forms published by the Insurance Services Office, which many insurers adapt, list protecting property from further damage among a policyholder's duties after a loss. The same section asks the policyholder to make reasonable and necessary repairs to protect the property. It also asks them to keep an accurate record of what those repairs cost. Individual policies vary, and the wording in your own contract is the one that governs.

Recent findings suggest that A paper or saved copy of your auto insurance ID card lets you prove coverage when Allstate $ALL's app or website won't load. Keep one printed card in the vehicle and one image stored directly on your phone. That way, your proof of insurance does not depend on a live connection.

Drivers in nearly every U.S. state must carry liability coverage. Police can ask to see proof of it during a traffic stop. Drivers involved in a crash typically exchange insurance details at the scene. A registration renewal or a trip to a motor vehicle office can also call for current proof of coverage.

Report a loss to Allstate $ALL as soon as you can, even if the app or website is down. Most insurance policies require prompt notice of a claim, and an outage does not pause that duty. A dated record of each attempt to report indicates you acted in good faith.

The requirement usually sits in a section of the policy with a title such as "what you must do after a loss" or "duties after loss." Wording varies, but phrases such as "promptly" or "as soon as practicable" are common. Those terms rarely name a fixed number of days. How quickly you must act depends on the policy language and the law in your state.

Read that section before assuming you have time. Some policies set separate, firmer deadlines for specific steps. A homeowners policy may require a signed, sworn proof of loss within a set period after the insurer asks for one. Many policies also include a clause limiting how long you have to sue the insurer over a disputed claim. State law can also affect these windows. Check both the policy text and your state's rules.

Scammers watch for service disruptions and pose as insurance staff to collect payment details, policy numbers or login credentials. During an Allstate $ALL outage, use only phone numbers and web addresses printed on your policy documents or listed on the organization's official website. Never give payment information to someone who contacts you first.

Industry observers note that an outage hands fraudsters a ready-made story. Policyholders may already expect something to be wrong with their account. A message claiming that a payment failed or a claim stalled can seem plausible as a result.

Recent findings suggest that an insurance policy is a contract, and a contract does not pause because a login page stops loading. When an insurer's app or website goes dark, that alone does not end the coverage a policyholder has paid for. The same goes for the duties the policy places on the customer, from reporting a loss to keeping coverage paid up.

According to recent reports, much of the routine business of insurance has moved to screens. Drivers pull up digital ID cards at traffic stops. Homeowners upload photos of damage, and premiums get paid with a few taps. That convenience can obscure how much still runs through older channels. Claims can be reported by phone. Agents keep offices and phone lines. Premium payments may be possible through an agent or by mail. Complaints can go to a state regulator that sits entirely outside the insurer's systems.

This guide covers what Allstate $ALL policyholders can do during an Allstate outage or any period when the manufacturer's digital tools are unavailable.

The most direct way to report a claim when Allstate $ALL's app or website is unavailable is by phone. Use the claims number printed on your insurance ID card or policy documents. A phone report does not depend on the insurer's digital tools.

Recent findings suggest that start with the paperwork you already have. Auto insurance ID cards typically list a claims contact. Policy packets, declarations pages, renewal notices and billing statements often carry contact details as well. Saved emails from the insurer may include the number too.

Recent findings suggest that paper records matter here. A policy folder in a desk drawer still works when screens and logins do not.

Gather your information before you dial. The representative will need your policy number to locate your coverage. Have it written down rather than stored only in an app you cannot open.

The basic facts of the loss come next. These include the date and approximate time, the exact location and a plain description of what happened. List what was damaged and whether anyone was hurt.

Auto claims call for more detail about the other parties. Write down the other driver's name, phone number, insurance company and policy number. Add their license plate and the make and model of their vehicle. If police responded, ask for the report number and keep it with your notes. Names and phone numbers of any witnesses belong in the same place.

Recent findings suggest that home and property claims need a different set of facts. Note the cause if you know it, such as a storm, a burst pipe, a fire or a break-in. Say whether the home is still safe to live in. For a theft, have the police report number ready.

It has been revealed that stick to what you know during the call. If a detail is uncertain, say so instead of guessing. You can add information as the claim moves forward.

It has been revealed that keep a written record of the conversation. Note the date and time of the call and the name of the representative. Ask for a claim or reference number and write it down before hanging up.

Ask what happens next. Find out when an adjuster is expected to contact you. Ask how to send photos and documents if the online portal cannot accept them.

An agent can do several useful things during a disruption. Agency staff can explain what a policy covers and what the deductible is. They can confirm whether a policy is active and help report a new loss. They can also describe the payment methods the office accepts.

There are limits to that role. Claims are typically investigated and settled by adjusters, not by the selling agent. An agent cannot promise a payout, rewrite policy terms or waive a deadline written into the contract. The agency may also depend on the same manufacturer systems that are down. Some lookups or document requests may have to wait until those systems return.

Visiting the office in person can help when phone lines are busy. Bring the policy number, a copy of the insurance ID card and any photos of damage. A short written timeline of what happened and when also helps. Ask the staff member to note the visit in the account file.

Write down the name of each person spoken to at the agency, along with the date and time of the conversation. Agency hours vary from office to office. An office may be closed when a loss happens. Outside those hours, the claims number printed on policy documents remains the main route.

Recent findings suggest that before any cleanup begins, photograph and film all damage to your home, vehicle or belongings. A visual record made right away reveals an adjuster the loss as it first looked. It also does not depend on an insurer's app or website being available.

Recent findings suggest that start wide. Take shots of the whole room, the full exterior wall or all four sides of the car. These show how far the damage extends. Then move in close on each problem area, such as a cracked windshield, a water stain on drywall or a dented door panel.

Industry observers note that A slow video walkthrough can capture detail that still photos miss. Narrate as you film. Name the room, the item and what happened. That ties each clip to a specific part of the claim later.

Industry observers note that most smartphones save the date and time in each photo's file data. Keep the original files rather than edited or cropped versions. Back them up to a computer, a cloud account or an email to yourself. That way the record survives if the phone is lost or damaged.

According to recent reports, after a car accident, document the scene as well as the vehicles. Useful images include the positions of the cars, road conditions, traffic signs, the other driver's license plate and any visible injuries. Write down the other driver's name, insurer and policy number. Add contact details for any witnesses. If police respond, note the officer's name and the report number.

For damage at home, build a written list of affected items as you photograph them. Include a description, the approximate age and the brand or model where known. Note where in the home each item was. Receipts, bank or card statements, product manuals and older photos of the items can help support their value.

Where it is safe, keep damaged items until an adjuster has inspected them or said they can go. Discarding a ruined appliance or a soaked rug too early can leave a claim with less proof. Spoiled food and anything that poses a health risk may need to go sooner. Photograph those items before disposal.

According to recent reports, store every photo, video and note in a single folder. When the app or claims website works again, or when you reach a representative by phone, the evidence is ready to share.

The duty has a practical side. Many homeowners policies exclude loss caused by neglect, meaning a failure to use all reasonable means to save and preserve property at and after a loss. A small roof leak left open for days can spread to drywall, flooring and insulation. An insurer may then treat that later damage as preventable.

Industry observers note that typical temporary measures are modest. They include covering a damaged roof with a tarp, boarding up a broken window or shutting off the main water valve after a burst pipe. Moving furniture and electronics away from standing water also counts. So does running fans or a dehumidifier to start drying out a wet room.

For a vehicle, the same logic applies on a smaller scale. Standard personal auto policies carry a similar duty to take reasonable steps after a loss to protect the covered vehicle from further loss. Taping plastic sheeting over a shattered window keeps rain out of the interior. Parking a car with a coolant leak or a damaged tire can prevent engine or wheel damage that the original accident did not cause.

Sources indicate that safety comes before any of this. Do not climb onto a wet or storm-damaged roof. Do not walk through standing water near live electrical outlets. For hazardous work, a licensed contractor or emergency water-mitigation organization can handle the job instead.

Keep the line between temporary and permanent work clear. Replacing a whole roof or tearing out cabinets before an adjuster inspects can make the claim harder to verify. Save invoices, receipts and payment records for every emergency purchase, from tarps and plywood to a contractor's call-out fee. Note the date of each step as well. A clear timeline is easier to present once the claim is reported.

If damage forces you out of your home, save every receipt for the extra costs of living somewhere else. Additional living expense coverage, often called loss of use, may reimburse those costs. It pays only if your policy includes it, and usually only for spending above your normal budget.

Sources indicate that this coverage is common in homeowners and renters policies. Standard homeowners forms usually list it as Coverage D, loss of use. Your declarations page shows whether you have it and what limit applies. Read that page before assuming any expense will be paid.

It has been revealed that the coverage typically applies when a covered loss, such as a fire or a burst pipe, makes the home unfit to live in. A loss the policy excludes generally won't trigger it. Flood damage under a standard homeowners policy is one example.

Reimbursement is generally based on the increase in your costs, not the full amount you spend. Mortgage or rent payments usually continue after a loss. A hotel bill on top of them is typically an added cost. Meals work differently. If your household normally spends a set amount on groceries, the claim usually covers the difference between that and what you now spend eating out.

That makes proof of your normal spending useful. Bank statements or past grocery receipts can show your typical monthly costs before the loss.

According to recent reports, keep receipts for hotel stays or short-term rentals, restaurant meals, laundry services and pet boarding. Save records of extra fuel or mileage if a temporary address lengthens your commute. Storage unit fees and the cost of moving into temporary housing also belong in the file.

Photograph each paper receipt as soon as you get it. Thermal receipt paper fades over time. Store the images in email or a cloud folder that doesn't depend on the insurer's app or website. A simple log with the date, amount, vendor and reason for each expense makes the claim easier to review.

Auto policies handle this separately. Rental reimbursement coverage is an optional add-on that may pay for a rental car while a covered vehicle is being repaired. If your auto declarations page doesn't list it, rental costs are generally your own.

Before committing to a large or long-term expense, such as a monthly lease, confirm with your agent or adjuster that it falls within your coverage. A written approval, even a short email, gives you a record to point to if the expense is questioned later.

A screenshot avoids that problem. Save the image to the phone's photo library or files folder. From there, it opens without an internet connection. A PDF downloaded from an online account works the same way. Zoom $ZM in on the saved copy to confirm that the policy number and dates are readable.

A printed card serves as the backup to the backup. Phones run out of battery, crack and get left at home. A paper card in the glovebox stays with the car no matter who is driving it. ID cards usually list the specific vehicle they cover. Households with more than one insured vehicle need a card for each car.

Recent findings suggest that insurance ID cards show effective and expiration dates. A card from an earlier policy term does not prove current coverage. Replace printed and saved copies each time the policy renews or a vehicle is added or removed.

Save the declarations page as well. It lists the coverages, limits, deductibles, drivers and vehicles on the policy. A stored PDF of it puts the policy details within reach when you report a claim or answer questions from another driver's insurer.

Rules on whether police and motor vehicle agencies accept electronic proof of insurance differ from state to state. A paper copy covers situations where a digital image is not accepted. Your state's motor vehicle agency can confirm the rules that apply where you drive.

If an outage stops you from paying a premium online, write down every attempt and keep proof of it. Then read your policy's grace period and cancellation language. Those terms, not the status of an app or website, decide what happens to a late payment.

A useful record is simple. Note the date and time of each try, the payment method you used and what happened. If a payment page shows an error message, take a screenshot that captures the date and time on your device. If a payment goes through by any route, save the confirmation number, receipt email or bank reference.

According to recent reports, check your bank or card statement before trying again. A payment that appeared to fail may still have been processed. A second attempt could then produce a duplicate charge. Policyholders enrolled in automatic payments should confirm that the scheduled withdrawal left their account on the expected date.

Recent findings suggest that A local Allstate $ALL agent's office may be able to accept a payment or explain other options while the online portal is down. Billing statements and policy paperwork generally list a mailing address for checks. If you mail a payment, use a service that documents the mailing date, such as certified mail through the U.S. Postal Service. Keep a copy of the check and the mailing receipt.

Industry observers note that grace period terms vary by policy, by type of coverage and by state. Some policies allow a window after the due date, and its length is not uniform. Do not assume one applies to your policy or matches the terms of an earlier policy. The billing and cancellation sections of the policy, along with any billing notice, set out the actual rules.

State insurance laws generally require an insurer to send written notice before canceling a policy for nonpayment. The notice rules, including how far in advance it must arrive, differ from state to state. A cancellation notice typically names a date by which payment must be received to keep coverage in force. Read any such notice closely if one arrives during or after a service disruption.

A lapse can carry consequences beyond the policy itself. Most states require drivers to carry auto liability insurance, and a gap in coverage can trigger state penalties. Mortgage lenders and auto lenders often require continuous coverage. If a borrower's policy lapses, a lender may buy coverage on the borrower's behalf, usually at a higher cost.

Recent findings suggest that the payment log matters if a billing dispute arises later. Dated records of on-time attempts through more than one channel give a policyholder something concrete to show the insurer.

Late notice can put a claim at risk. Courts in many states apply what is known as the notice-prejudice rule. Under it, an insurer generally must show that a delay harmed its ability to investigate before denying a claim for lateness. Not every state follows that rule, and it may not cover every type of policy. Reporting early keeps the question from arising.

Recent findings suggest that if digital channels fail, use another route and document it. Write down the date, time, method and outcome of every attempt, including calls that went unanswered. Save screenshots of error messages showing the app or site was unavailable. These records help show that the delay did not start with you.

Written notice adds a second layer of proof. An email to your agent carries its own timestamp, and a dated letter serves the same purpose. Include your policy number, the date and location of the loss and a short description. Sending a letter by USPS Certified Mail with a return receipt gives you proof of delivery.

Some losses carry reporting duties outside the insurer. Auto policies commonly require you to notify police after a vehicle theft. Uninsured motorist coverage for a hit-and-run often requires a police report as well. File those reports promptly, and keep each report number with your claim records.

It has been revealed that if Allstate $ALL does not respond to a claim, a payment problem or a coverage question within a reasonable time, a policyholder can file a complaint with their state's insurance regulator. Every state runs an office that accepts consumer complaints about insurers.

According to recent reports, insurance in the U.S. is regulated mainly at the state level rather than by a single federal agency. Congress affirmed that arrangement in the McCarran-Ferguson Act, passed in 1945. The agency that oversees an Allstate policy therefore depends on the state where the policy was issued. The location of the manufacturer's headquarters does not decide it.

The office goes by different names. Many states call it the department of insurance. Others use a division of insurance or an insurance commissioner's office. In New York, insurance oversight sits with the Department of Financial Services. The National Association of Insurance Commissioners keeps a directory of state regulators on its website. The official state government site will also list the correct agency.

Industry observers note that A complaint makes the most sense after direct contact has failed. That means the policyholder has already tried the claims line, the local agent or written correspondence. It also means they have not received an answer or a fair resolution. Regulators generally expect consumers to give the insurer a chance to fix the problem first.

Recent findings suggest that A useful complaint is specific. It should include the policy number and the claim number, if one exists. It should also name anyone the policyholder spoke with and give a timeline of each contact attempt. Copies of letters, emails, photos and receipts help a reviewer see what happened. A clear statement of the outcome the policyholder wants also helps the review.

Most state departments accept complaints through an online form. Many also take them by mail or phone. After a complaint arrives, the department typically forwards it to the insurer and asks for a written response. A reviewer then checks whether the tech giant followed the policy terms and state law.

A regulator does not act as the policyholder's lawyer. It usually cannot settle a factual dispute over how much a claim is worth. Complaint records still serve a purpose beyond the individual case. State regulators use them to spot patterns in how an insurer treats customers. Recurring problems can lead to a formal market conduct examination of the company.

It has been revealed that caller ID offers little protection. Phone numbers can be spoofed to display a legitimate company name or a familiar area code. Email sender names can be faked the same way. A display name that matches the insurer is not proof the message came from it.

In a recent development, the safer move is to end the contact and start a upcoming one yourself. Hang up or close the message. Then dial the number on your ID card, declarations page or a past bill. A local agent you already work with is another route. If the original request was genuine, someone on that verified line can confirm it.

In a recent development, links in unexpected texts and emails call for the same caution. Typing the insurer's address directly into a browser avoids lookalike domains that differ by a single letter or an added word. Passwords and one-time security codes should never go to anyone who calls or writes asking for them.

Recent findings suggest that suspected scams can be reported. The Federal Trade Commission collects fraud reports from consumers. The National Insurance Crime Bureau accepts tips about insurance fraud. Many state insurance departments also run fraud units that take reports of people impersonating insurers.

Sources indicate that anyone who already shared card or bank details should contact the bank or card issuer right away to flag the account. Keep a copy of the suspicious message, along with the number or address it came from.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rinnai has debuted a newly introduced lineup of electric heat pump water heaters that adds wifi controls and more installation options to an appliance that can cut the energy needed for hot showers.

The REHPW series comes in 50-, 65-, and 80-gallon sizes. It builds on Rinnai’s existing REHP lineup, with changes designed to make the units easier to install, monitor, and maintain.

According to recent reports, heat pump water heaters pull heat from the surrounding air and transfer it into the tank. Moving that heat requires less electricity than producing it with conventional electric resistance elements. There’s no fuel combustion at the appliance, although emissions from its electricity supply depend on the grid.

Industry observers note that rinnai lists a Uniform Energy Factor, or UEF, of 3.75 for the 50-gallon model and 4.0 for the two larger versions. Higher numbers mean greater efficiency under standardized testing; actual bills depend on electricity rates, hot water use, and installation conditions.

The lineup delivers up to 91 gallons of hot water in the first hour, depending on tank size. That rating includes both stored hot water and what the unit can heat during that hour – useful context when several people take consecutive showers.

There are five operating modes, 4.5 kW backup heating elements, and a variable-speed fan designed to keep noise down. The heat pump can operate with ambient air as low as 37°F.

Installation is where some of the more practical upgrades show up.

According to recent reports, the upcoming Rinnai heat pump water heater units have water connections on both the top and side, giving installers more options for connecting existing plumbing. Both the air intake and exhaust are on top, allowing zero side clearance where Rinnai’s installation requirements permit.

An optional ducting kit adds flexibility for tighter spaces. Carrying handles help with moving the tank into place, and the air filter slides out horizontally from the side for cleaning.

Rinnai has also added a third tank temperature sensor to the 50- and 80-gallon models to help manage hot water delivery.

It has been revealed that wifi adds remote monitoring and control. Rinnai’s updated Central app supports the REHPW series, including scheduling and tools to use time-of-use electricity rates to manage energy use.

The units also carry CTA-2045 AC Level 2 certification for demand response. That gives compatible utility programs a way to communicate with the water heater and adjust its electricity use. Rinnai claims the certification can help qualify homeowners for local and state utility demand-response rebates; availability depends on the program.

Sources indicate that the series is Energy Star certified, meets NEEA Tier 4 requirements, and complies with California’s Title 24 requirements, including JA13, according to Rinnai. Warranty coverage includes 10 years for the tank and other parts, plus one year for labor.

It has been revealed that I’m very happy with my hybrid heat pump water heater. I run it in heat pump only mode in summer and it helps cool the house for free. For anyone on the fence, especially your utility offers a rebate, it’s definitely worth looking at.

In a recent development, rinnai directs buyers to an installer for pricing, so the upfront cost – and how much a local rebate might offset it – will require a quote. However, the REHP series price on Amazon hovers around the $2,000 mark.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The chief executive of one of the world’s leading fashion brands has mentioned that the intense and often slow process of craftswomen and men making products by hand has become a vital skill in a world of online “instant gratification.”.

Leena Nair, the CEO of Chanel, said that business leaders are living through an “unprecedented” period of transformation and fragility, adding that it was time to prioritize human ingenuity and talent.

It has been revealed that “Macro-economic shifts, huge leaps in AI and technology and geopolitical instability, these are challenges affecting all sectors,” she told the annual gala dinner of the French Chamber of Great Britain, which brings together U.K. and French business executives, policy makers, and cultural leaders.

Recent findings suggest that “And in this context of disruption, the power of creation and beauty has never been more vital or more precious. Creation and beauty have been vital sources of inspiration and joy for thousands of years. They’re even more precious today in a world of constant instant gratification, constant overstimulation, and infinite touch points.”.

Nair, who has been Chanel CEO since 2022, saw the luxury brand return to growth last year, led by an increase in sales in America. Global revenues rose by 1.8% compared with 2024 to $19.3 billion, while operating profits rose 5.2% to $4.7 billion.

Nair said there was a growing body of scientific evidence that revealed that exposure to art and human-led creative work led to higher levels of happiness and performance.

Sources indicate that “This growing body of academic research shows how encounters with beauty correlate directly to a greater sense of human flourishing at work and in life,” she mentioned. “In recent years, we see growing scientific evidence of the improving impact that arts and culture has on physical and mental well-being.”.

“In this context of disruption, the power of creation and beauty has never been more vital or more precious”.

Over 95% of Chanel’s customers are women, Nair said, adding that “beauty” is a very vital driver of how people respond to the world around them. She said that one customer who had been through surgery said that buying crafted products was part of her recovery.

“Surgeons tell me this all the time, that when surgery is over they know the women are back to normal when they ask to put on their makeup for the first time,” she mentioned.

Sources indicate that many leaders of luxury brands often feel ignored when it comes to policy debates about economic growth. In the U.K., the end of foreign visitors being able to shop without incurring the national sales tax has caused controversy. In the U.S., new tariffs targeting luxury goods have unsettled markets.

Recent findings suggest that “Luxury is an economic powerhouse, it’s a cultural powerhouse and an emotional powerhouse,” Nair remarked. “To put that scale into context, European high-end luxury brands generate a trillion dollars in business every year. That’s 5% of Europe’s GDP. “It’s not a niche sector. More than 2 million people work in the sector across Europe.”.

Chanel works with the King’s Foundation, King Charles III’s organization that supports the retention and development of traditional skills.

“It looks simple, but to do a pleated skirt takes eight hours of pushing a cardboard mold back and forth by two talented artisans doing it the right way,” Nair said, arguing that Chanel continues to invest in “skills that will otherwise be lost, working with extraordinary artisans and partners, many of whom we have worked with for generations.”.

Etzioni on AI: The outage conspiracy theories are wrong — our rush to patch and upgrade is the culprit

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (853 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Geekwire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • by Oren Etzioni on Nov 22, 2026 at 7:04 amNovember 22, 2026 at 7:06 am.
  • In less than a week, Microsoft email went dark around the world, the FAA halted every departure in the country, Chase payments stalled, Apple’s services faltered and the NSA’s internal network went down.
  • Recent findings suggest that attackers typically announce when they’ve hit you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Oren Etzioni on Nov 22, 2026 at 7:04 amNovember 22, 2026 at 7:06 am.

In less than a week, Microsoft email went dark around the world, the FAA halted every departure in the country, Chase payments stalled, Apple’s services faltered and the NSA’s internal network went down. Sen. Josh Hawley said that if this was all a coincidence, “it’s like the greatest coincidence in the history of the world.” Yet intelligence and law enforcement officials told Congress they’ve found no evidence that anyone was attacking us.

Recent findings suggest that attackers typically announce when they’ve hit you. Terrorists claim credit. Criminals issue ransom notes and often brag as well: the hackers who crippled MGM’s casino systems in 2023 told TechCrunch within days. None of this month’s outages came with any of that.

It has been revealed that could a state actor be flexing its cyber capabilities to warn us? China’s Volt Typhoon hackers kept access to U.S. critical infrastructure for at least five years before anyone made it public, positioning themselves to disrupt it in a future crisis. However, hackers who are that patient don’t blow their cover by knocking out the world’s email. A warning shot also works only if the target knows who fired it, and we don’t have a credible suspect for a shooter here.

Each outage has a separate origin tracing back to the organization’s own systems: a new router a contractor was installing for the FAA, a bug Microsoft shipped in July, a software bug at Chase, an internal update at Apple, a patch at the NSA. To stage that, a single attacker would have to break into three companies and two federal agencies, disguise every intrusion as a routine mistake and leave nothing for investigators to find.

A far more credible root cause is the patch treadmill set at too high a speed: AI is finding security holes faster than anyone can safely fix them, and the rush to patch and upgrade is making everything more fragile. Think of an immune system in overdrive. It fights off infection, and sometimes it attacks healthy tissue. This month’s outages were a flare-up.

On Nov. 17, the startup Calif disclosed Java4Shell, a critical flaw in Java, the software platform used by government agencies and about 90% of Fortune 500 companies. Calif found it with OpenAI’s GPT-6 Cyber model. Oracle shipped a patch the same day, and a federal alert urged organizations to “immediately patch.”.

Last month the same startup used OpenAI models to find a flaw in PHP, the programming language behind an estimated 70% of websites, and Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton tied the NSA’s outage to the patching that followed. Microsoft alone fixed 1,413 vulnerabilities in October, more than its previous record for an entire year.

Sources indicate that AI is forcing faster fixes. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says his company’s outage came from a dormant bug, but he warned this week that AI-driven patching could bring more instability. AI has “allowed us to find these bugs and fix these bugs, but that means you’ve got to then patch them, and that creates instability,” he told CNBC.

Recent findings suggest that A patch for a critical bank system might once have been tested for a week, he remarked at the Newly introduced York Times DealBook Summit. Now it “needs to go instantly from being available to being patched in production because it’s being exploited in the wild.”.

It has been revealed that the FBI warned on Nov. 13 that criminals and state-backed hackers are already using ARTEX, an open-source AI tool built for testing a manufacturer’s own defenses, with some intrusions going from first targeting to administrator-level access in under three hours. So the patching can’t slow down. Nobody would give up their immune system to avoid a flare-up.

Recent findings suggest that it will get worse before it gets better. Calif’s CEO, Thai Duong, expects Java4Shell to threaten systems that don’t update for the next five to 10 years.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, the AI that finds flaws like this one is spreading. Open-weight models, which anyone can download and run without safeguards, trail the most advanced models on cyber tasks by only four to seven months, according to the UK AI Security Institute. Every month will bring more bugs, more emergency patches and more flare-ups.

It has been revealed that there’s a finite amount of code in Windows, iOS and Chrome, and every bug AI finds and fixes there is one an attacker can’t use. Partners in Anthropic’s Project Glasswing, a program to secure critical software before AI can be turned against it, found more than 10,000 high- or critical-severity bugs in its first month.

In a recent development, former Microsoft security staffer Angela Gunn sees a hopeful sign: more and more unrelated researchers are turning up the same bugs, which suggests the supply is finite. Fixing still lags finding, but the giants have the money and people to catch up. Within a year or two, I expect Windows, iOS and Chrome to be more secure than they’ve ever been.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • And it only works inside Tesla’s Robotaxi service areas in Texas and Florida, the same geofences that have turned out to be significantly smaller than what Tesla advertises.
  • Tesla’s official Robotaxi account declared the invites on X on Friday with screenshots of the order page and the invitation email.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla is now inviting “select customers” to buy a Cybercab for personal use at $29,990, but the car won’t move unless you also pay $299 a month for an “Autonomy Subscription.”.

And it only works inside Tesla’s Robotaxi service areas in Texas and Florida, the same geofences that have turned out to be significantly smaller than what Tesla advertises.

Tesla’s official Robotaxi account declared the invites on X on Friday with screenshots of the order page and the invitation email.

The order page lists the Cybercab at $29,990 before taxes, with an estimated delivery of December 2026 in Austin, Texas. You need to put down a $1,000 non-refundable deposit to order.

In a recent development, the subscription isn’t optional. It’s pre-checked on the order page at $299 per month, with one month included, and the fine print states “Subscription and regular vehicle maintenance required to operate.”.

The email is even more direct. Its asterisk reads: “Only available in supported service areas. Subscription required for operation.”.

Sources indicate that the rest is what we already knew. Two seats, a 21-inch center touchscreen, 20.1 cubic feet of cargo space, and no steering wheel or pedals. Tesla calls it “fully autonomous” and says you’ll “manage your ride in the app.”.

Musk had promised a Cybercab “below $30,000” when he unveiled it in 2024. He technically hit it. He just didn’t mention the $3,588 a year it takes to use it. Over five years, that’s about $47,600 for a two-seater, before insurance, maintenance, taxes, and charging.

Tesla runs its Robotaxi service in eight cities: Austin, Dallas, Houston, Fort Worth, and San Antonio in Texas, and Miami, Orlando, and Tampa in Florida. That’s where a Cybercab can operate. Everywhere else, it’s a $30,000 sculpture in your driveway.

Sources indicate that and those service areas aren’t what Tesla states they are. Independent tracker Koby Pierce tested thousands of addresses in the Robotaxi app and found that the areas where Tesla actually accepts pickups and drop-offs are only 59% to 78% of the advertised geofences in the six cities he checked. In Austin, the very city where Tesla is delivering these cars, it’s about 59%.

Railroad crossings are a big reason why. In Houston, the creator of Robotaxi Tracker found the app quoting about 40 minutes to go two blocks downtown because the vehicle appeared to route around rail crossings. Tesla also lists San Antonio’s airport inside its polygon but doesn’t serve it.

Recent findings suggest that then there’s the regulatory cloud. NHTSA has ordered Tesla to prove under oath that a car with no brake pedal meets federal safety standards that require one. Tesla answered on October 30 and asked that the entire response be kept confidential. NHTSA hasn’t ruled. Tesla is now selling the car to consumers anyway.

Recent findings suggest that I think this is going to be a total mess. It looks like Tesla is only doing this by invitation and delivering it in Austin to prove they can deliver an “unsupervised” vehicle in 2026.

Tesla is going to sell these to fans who are excited about owning a self-driving car, and many of them will find out the limitations aren’t worth $299 a month on top of a $30,000 car.

Recent findings suggest that sure, if your monthly Uber bill is well over $300 and you live and work deep inside the geofence, maybe the math works on paper. Until you realize you have to park it somewhere once you get to your destination. Or that it can’t take you to a friend’s place two neighborhoods over. Or that a 15-minute drive turns into an hour because the car won’t cross a train track. With an Uber or a Waymo, that’s someone else’s problem. With a Cybercab, you’re paying for the privilege.

No point trying to calculate what it will cost over X years. Tesla can change that monthly fee at will anyway (and shall be expected to, considering their overall pricing history).

In a recent development, and here’s the part that makes no sense to me. The Cybercab runs on the same AI4 computer as the current Model Y. Tesla already runs unsupervised Model Y Robotaxis in these same geofences. So why can’t the Model Y owners who already paid for “Full Self-Driving” get unsupervised operation in those same zones? Wouldn’t be even easier to turn that on these vehicles which have accumulated much more data? Tesla keeps pushing that to “next year,” currently around Q2 2027, while asking people to buy a new two-seater that can do nothing else.

In a recent development, if the tech works unsupervised in Austin, turn it on for the Model Y owners in Austin. If it doesn’t, why should anyone pay $47,000 over five years for a car that only works where Tesla notes it does?

Like with every other Tesla product lately, the delivered version is going to be a lot more disappointing than the one that was sold on stage.

XRP has completed a short-term golden cross against Bitcoin, giving bulls a fresh technical signal as the cryptocurrency eyes a retest of $1.

In a recent development, the 50 MA rose above the 200 MA on the 3-hour chart, completing a golden cross, as XRP saw relative outperformance against Bitcoin. The timing of the golden cross remains surprising given the current selling in the market.

At the time of writing, XRP was down 5.83% in the last 24 hours to $0.923, giving back most of a rally that sharply took it past $1 after Jensen Huang returned as CEO of Nvidia.

According to recent reports, on Monday, Nvidia shocked the markets with the surprise announcement of Jensen Huang returning as the CEO of the popular tech and AI company. For crypto traders, the initial response looked extremely encouraging as most tokens sharply rose. However, the rebound began fading, with most cryptocurrencies seeing visible losses in an ongoing selloff in the early Tuesday session.

Bitcoin was down 5.23% in the last 24 hours to $60,298, with total liquidations across the crypto market reaching $596 million.

The $1 price point remains significant for XRP as it is slightly above the lower boundary of the channel in which XRP traded in recent months.

According to recent reports, XRP failed to break above the $1.55 resistance at the top of the channel and completed a full reversal toward the channel’s lower boundary at $0.99. XRP broke below this key support level in the past week, cascading to a low of $0.86, last seen in November 2024.

This drop also coincided with a death cross on the daily chart of its USD pairing, the first such occurrence in 2026. For the bearish outlook to weaken, XRP would need to reclaim $0.99 as support.

XRP's attempt to return above $1 has met a brick wall since mid-November. On November 18, XRP's price rise stopped exactly at $1, before it started to decline again.

In a recent development, on November 23, 2026, XRP tried to break above $1 again after reaching $1.02, but bulls could not hold the momentum. If the price goes above $1, XRP will target $1.21 and $1.40. On the downside, key support is expected near $0.80 and $0.64.

Hackers breach Air Force cloud as cyberattacks hit the CIA, FBI and Pentagon

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1183 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Qz

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Reuters tracked 2026 intrusions at the Air Force, CIA, FBI, Pentagon and more.
  • According to recent reports, A government hack is often pictured as one dramatic event, but in 2026 break-ins at U.S.
  • Industry observers note that what ties these breaches together is not a single attacker but how little is known about what the intruders took.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Reuters tracked 2026 intrusions at the Air Force, CIA, FBI, Pentagon and more. Five incidents, and who did it is still unclear.

According to recent reports, A government hack is often pictured as one dramatic event, but in 2026 break-ins at U.S. agencies became public one after another. President Trump confirmed in a Fox News interview on Nov. 21 that hackers had broken into an FBI database, according to CNBC, and within days the public learned of a breach at an intelligence agency as well. Each new disclosure arrived before the last one had been explained. The targets also went beyond spy and military agencies to departments that most people rarely connect with national security.

Industry observers note that what ties these breaches together is not a single attacker but how little is known about what the intruders took. No one has spelled out exactly what they got at the intelligence agency, according to the Honolulu Star-Advertiser, or which records they removed from the FBI database. Justin Sherman, a senior associate at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, claims no database hack should be waved off as routine because each one connects to others, according to TIME. A breach in 2026 is best judged by what the intruders could reach, not by a confirmed count of stolen files.

Reuters lists the major cyber intrusions of 2026 into U.S. government agencies and other targets. Intruders got into the Air Force's main cloud platform and into a research tool that the CIA shares with the country's top intelligence office, while other attackers went after dozens of commercial ships. What each intruder could reach shows where the real exposure lies, from weapons data and intelligence tools to police records, personnel files and shipping.

Hackers who broke into Cloud One, the Air Force's flagship computing platform, got into the part of the system that manages the entire platform rather than a single application. They reached its control plane by exploiting a software flaw, according to TNW. From there, the intruders potentially exposed aircraft and radar data, along with data from a munitions system used at more than 200 sites.

Recent findings suggest that getting into the controls does not prove that anyone read the data behind them. No one has shown that the intruders looked at any aircraft or parts records, or publicly identified who got in. U.S. Cyber Command is assessing the damage. The Air Force stated in a statement to Reuters that it "does not comment on the security posture, vulnerabilities or operational status of specific networks and systems.".

It has been revealed that whether or not the hackers took anything, the Air Force has already lost the use of its flagship cloud for fresh work. The service's initiative to shift its back-office programs onto the platform is on hold, and the software already hosted there can no longer receive updates.

In a recent development, A breach at an intelligence agency makes most people picture stolen secrets, but these hackers got into the tool the agencies use to read the open world. They accessed the open-source scanning system of the CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, which scans unclassified, publicly available material.

The only public reassurance is narrow. The Office of the Director of National Intelligence remarked there were "no disruptions to critical capabilities or classified systems." That statement rules out breakage, not entry.

Early signs point to possible Chinese involvement, but no account of how the intruders got in has been made public, so China remains a suspicion rather than a confirmed finding.

The hackers reached a tool two intelligence agencies use, and who did it is still unsettled.

Sources indicate that at the Defense Manpower Data Center, hackers went after the people who serve and support the military, not its weapons or its intelligence tools. An earlier intrusion into the center affected 2.76 million living people, a fraction of the more than 60 million people the agency held records on in fiscal 2024.

Recent findings suggest that for the people in those files, the risk is personal. The exposed details include birthdates and military specialties, which together link who a person is to the work that person does for the military.

Intruders were inside the center's systems for months before anyone noticed. Unauthorized access began in October 2025, and no one found the weakness that let them in until July 16, 2026. No one has publicly named the attacker.

The people in those files may not learn for years whether anyone has used their details.

At Cloud One, the hackers did harm simply by getting in, and any theft that comes to light would only add to it.

Industry observers note that the FBI suffered two breaches in one fall. The first came in September, when intruders took data on FBI employees and forced the agency to shut down part of its operations until the breach was resolved. The second reached the National Crime Information Center, a shared criminal-justice system that police well beyond the FBI rely on, so a breach there becomes a problem for every department that checks a name against it.

This breach puts everyday police records at risk, so what matters is whether departments can still trust what they look up. The September theft was the work of a cybercrime group called ShinyHunters, which shows criminal hackers, not only foreign governments, are getting inside federal law enforcement. No one has publicly named who broke into the criminal database.

When Trump talked about the database break-in, he spoke of a possible upside rather than the damage, suggesting the breach might turn up evidence of voter fraud. "I always like to put things on a positive spin," Trump stated.

Police nationwide still rely on a system whose breach the government has acknowledged but not explained.

According to recent reports, the 2026 breaches reached civilian departments and commercial ships as well as spy and military systems. Personnel data leaked from the Department of Homeland Security, intruders broke into the Treasury Department, and as many as 50 ships carrying oil and other explosive cargo are believed to have been hit by cyberattacks. No details have been made public on what the intruders reached at either department.

Iran is the primary suspect in the ship attacks, according to The Wall Street Journal, and U.S. officials also see Russia as a possible culprit. A Trump administration official disputed that, saying the U.S. has found no evidence of Iranian involvement and that four attacks amounted to little more than a minor nuisance. Coast Guard cyber teams have responded to at least four of the ships as they approached U.S. ports.

Industry observers note that the attackers are exploiting a flaw in Fortinet $FTNT routers that are popular in the maritime industry. Some ships also received bomb threats, and the attacks come as Iran continues to mount physical attacks against ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

The ship attacks can't easily turn a tanker into a weapon, but a hacked vessel can still stall a cargo of fuel.

Latest Update: Clock Ticking on Zcash’s Sprout Pool: 22,263 ZEC Unmoved Ahead of NU7 Lock

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1213 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that daily pool data reveals Sprout holders moved more than 300 ZEC out in a September rush, then almost stopped.
  • Unless someone acts in the next few days, nearly all of what remains will be unspendable at block 3,543,405.
  • Most coverage of Zcash's upcoming Sprout freeze quotes the same figure, about 22,000 ZEC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Industry observers note that daily pool data reveals Sprout holders moved more than 300 ZEC out in a September rush, then almost stopped. The last withdrawal was on October 19.

Unless someone acts in the next few days, nearly all of what remains will be unspendable at block 3,543,405.

Most coverage of Zcash's upcoming Sprout freeze quotes the same figure, about 22,000 ZEC. That number is accurate, but it is a single snapshot. It doesn't show whether the people who own those coins are doing anything about the deadline.

We checked the pool every day, and the answer so far is no.

Recent findings suggest that according to ZecStats' daily value-pool records, Sprout has held exactly 22,263.34162335 ZEC since October 19. That is 11 straight days, and more than 12,000 blocks, without a single zatoshi leaving the pool. Our October 25 piece recorded the drop from 22,309 ZEC to 22,263 ZEC. Since then the balance hasn't moved.

In a recent development, zecStats publishes a daily CSV of every Zcash value pool, using the last block of each UTC day. Its figures follow the valuePools field that a full node returns through the getblockchaininfo call. The archive starts on July 30, 2026, and gives a 92-day picture of the Sprout pool.

It has been revealed that across those 92 days, about 374 ZEC, or 1.65% of the pool, left Sprout. That is an average of roughly 4 ZEC a day. The average hides the real pattern, though: the pool moved on only 15 of the 92 days.

Most of the withdrawals came in a few large transfers in September:.

Sources indicate that together with smaller moves on August 31, September 17 and September 19, the 30 days to September 29 saw 310.5 ZEC leave Sprout. That is about 10 ZEC a day.

In a recent development, october was much quieter. Apart from one withdrawal of 46.05 ZEC on October 19, the month's activity was small change:.

Since October 19, there has been no movement at all.

At September's pace, about 70 ZEC more would leave before activation. At October's pace, it would be well under 15 ZEC. On the last 11 days' pace, the answer is zero.

According to recent reports, the deadline is set in ZIP 259, which defines how the NU7 network upgrade is deployed. It sets the mainnet activation height at 3,543,405.

It has been revealed that NU7 does not introduce a new transaction format. Instead, after activation, version 4 transactions become invalid, while versions 5 and 6 remain valid. Sprout's design is the problem. As ZIP 259 puts it: "Because Sprout transfers can only be represented by version 4 transactions, funds remaining in the Sprout pool become unspendable.".

Recent findings suggest that the coins would not be destroyed, and NU7 does not change Zcash's supply cap. They would simply be stuck in a pool that no valid transaction can spend from. Today the stranded amount would be 22,263 ZEC, about 0.13% of the roughly 17.01 million ZEC in circulation.

The rest of the upgrade is larger:.

ZIP 259 also skips Zcash's usual three-month gap between the first supporting software release and activation. Operators running unsupported software could stay online and follow a pre-NU7 chain.

Recent findings suggest that as of ZecStats' latest revision on October 30 at 13:09 UTC, the chain was at block 3,535,877. That leaves 7,528 blocks until activation.

According to recent reports, in October, the network averaged about 1,147 blocks a day, or one roughly every 75.3 seconds. At that rate, block 3,543,405 arrives around 02:00–03:00 UTC on November 6. That is the evening of November 5 in the Americas and the early hours of November 6 in Europe and Africa.

Recent findings suggest that small changes in block times could move that window by a few hours. Holders who plan to move funds on the final day risk missing the cutoff.

Industry observers note that in practice, getting funds out of Sprout means sending a version 4 transaction that moves them into a newer pool before activation. Consumers need software that can still build Sprout transactions and a synced node or wallet that recognizes their old notes.

The September withdrawals show that some holders are still paying attention. Several were round amounts, such as 99.998 ZEC, which is consistent with someone moving 100 ZEC and paying a fee. The 11-day pause since October 19 suggests something else: most of the remaining 22,263 ZEC may belong to keys that are lost, forgotten or no longer used.

That has been part of the debate about Sprout for years. A pool that has been shrinking slowly since Zcash's early days is now on a fixed timetable. The daily data indicates that most of its remaining balance is not being moved.

Every report that cites "about 22,000 ZEC at risk" is technically correct. The more useful figure for anyone tracking the upgrade is the rate of change, and right now that rate is zero.

The useful thing to watch over the next week is whether the Sprout line in ZecStats' daily data moves again before block 3,543,405. If it doesn't, Zcash will activate NU7 with about 22,263 ZEC permanently locked in its first shielded pool. That would be one of the largest deliberate freezes of user funds by any major blockchain upgrade, and nearly all of it would be coins whose owners did not move them in time.

5 trends that will define 2027—and how to invest in them

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that heraclitus, the Greek philosopher, is often credited with the idea that the only constant in life is change.
  • In 2024, it appeared that pandemic-era inflation had been tamed, and the Federal Reserve responded with a series of cuts to its benchmark interest rate.
  • According to recent reports, this is glum news for homebuyers and the real estate industry, and for sectors including AI, which count on cheap credit to keep their businesses humming.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that heraclitus, the Greek philosopher, is often credited with the idea that the only constant in life is change. He was writing around 500 BC, but he could just as easily have been describing 2027, a year poised to bring seismic shifts in politics, technology, markets, and the way we live and work. Some of what’s coming is already in plain sight, like the AI revolution. Other forces are quieter but could prove just as consequential, including a likely surge in solar construction. Here are the five trends Fortune believes will define the coming year, and how investors can position themselves for each.

In 2024, it appeared that pandemic-era inflation had been tamed, and the Federal Reserve responded with a series of cuts to its benchmark interest rate. This optimism didn’t last, however, and price shocks from tariffs and the Iran war led the Fed to boost rates in 2026. The central bank is expected to continue on this path.

According to recent reports, this is glum news for homebuyers and the real estate industry, and for sectors including AI, which count on cheap credit to keep their businesses humming. But high interest rates are not bad for everyone. Beneficiaries include individual savers, who can look forward to higher income, and major banks whose business involves lending money.

Sources indicate that while banks tend to earn more from loans when rates are higher, it is the “goliath” banks that do best in these environments, said Mike Mayo, head of U.S. large-cap bank research at Wells Fargo Securities. For 2027, Mayo said JPMorgan Chase (JPM) and Bank of America (BAC), in particular, appear poised for a strong year based on bullish guidance they have issued. But he cautions that high interest rates only act as a tailwind up to a point—and that a rapid series of hikes would put larger portions of the economy under strain, counteracting the positive effect of higher interest rates for banks.

It has been revealed that mayo dismissed concerns over upcoming technologies, such as yield-seeking AI agents that could threaten the deposit base of the biggest banks such as Citigroup (C) and Wells Fargo (WFC). “The death of large banks has been exaggerated for 50 years,” he mentioned. “Their deposit franchises have become bigger over time, and the reason is trust. Trust is more key than Big Tech.”.

Sources indicate that this trust in established financial institutions, along with substantial banks’ aversion to risk in general, are likely to serve the banks especially well at a time of mounting unease over cybersecurity—the result of a spate of recent incidents, including ones involving rogue AI agents. In this context, the “goliath” banks may draw investors looking for a safe and steady play.

And while their performance trailed the broader S&P 500 in 2026, the Significant Four banks delivered on another attribute that investors value: large and reliable dividends.

It’s been about four years since OpenAI’s launch of ChatGPT set off a massive rally in AI stocks. Some investors are getting jitters about the scope of the AI build-out amid fears that it’s a bubble—especially after the blue wave midterms elected a slew of Democrats on promises to rein in the AI industry. Still, the tech behemoths at the center of the boom—including Meta Platforms, Microsoft, and Amazon—are going full speed.

In this environment, looking for opportunities is not about deciding whether artificial intelligence is the future (spoiler alert: It is). The real question is which companies are positioned to succeed, no matter the pace of the AI build-out.

In this context, Bernstein senior analyst Stacy Rasgon likes the chipmaker Broadcom (AVGO) because its stock is “very, very cheap,” he told Fortune. The stock, like that of other chipmakers, sold off sharply in late 2026 as investors questioned how long the AI spending frenzy can last, even though earnings expectations remain strong.

Sources indicate that fellow chipmaker Nvidia’s shares took a major hit in November following revelations that its CEO, Jensen Huang, had acknowledged an affair, while the organization opened an investigation into reports that he had been targeted by Chinese intelligence. Huang resigned from the company he cofounded four days later.

In a recent development, applied Materials (AMAT) is another stock that may offer considerable upside. The company sells equipment to manufacture chips, positioning Applied Materials to benefit from infrastructure investments in advanced processors, memory, and chip packaging. “It’s very clear to me that we need a lot more equipment,” noted Rasgon.

That doesn’t mean these companies won’t face potential headwinds in 2027. Arun Sundaram, an investment strategist at CFRA, points to potential energy bottlenecks and concerns that higher interest rates could make AI financing more expensive. He cites political pushback against data center construction as another potential obstacle—opposition that will only increase as Democrats, many of whom have been vocal critics of the AI industry, take power in Congress.

Still, analysts like Rasgon remain optimistic. He pointed to third-quarter earnings from Big Tech, which included more AI spending and a surge in cloud revenues. “As it turns out, a lot of these companies may be more profitable than people thought. They’re actually generating money,” he said. “From a fundamental level, we’ll probably see sustainability in spending … Whether or not sentiment from a stock standpoint is going to buy into that or not, I don’t know yet. But that’s going to be the key debate.”.

Most of our recommendations point you toward stocks or sectors to buy. When it comes to the defense industry in 2027 you might be well served to do the opposite: Stay on the sidelines. Russia’s invasion of Ukraine dragged into its fifth year in February 2026. That same month, the U.S. and Israel launched a war against Iran, triggering retaliatory attacks across the Middle East. By early summer, there was anxious talk in Washington, D.C., about depleted stocks of missiles and other munitions.

In such an environment, investors might expect the shares of large defense companies to be soaring. That’s not the case. Even as demand for weapons has grown and a slew of techy startups have entered the sector, the stock prices of the massive military contractors known as the “primes”—including RTX, Northrop Grumman, and General Dynamics—have largely flailed. Only one of these companies, Lockheed Martin, outperformed the S&P. Shares of Boeing, which has a sizable division that sells to the military, lagged the index by 30%.

High interest rates are glum news for homebuyers and the real estate and AI industries, but individual savers and substantial banks can benefit—up to a point.

The reason for this lackluster performance is ongoing uncertainty over U.S. defense spending, said Peter Arment, a senior analyst at Baird. While the Pentagon and President Donald Trump are keen to pass a massive allocation for the military, it’s unclear where the money to pay for it would come from. Meanwhile, many in the incoming freshman class of Democrats vocally oppose Trump’s military policies.

While there is a tradition of bipartisan support for the military in Congress, this may not translate into a major defense bill in 2027, Arment noted. Instead, lawmakers may rely on ad hoc measures that don’t include significant military spending.

We’ve all heard the buzz about GLP-1s, the blockbuster category of drugs that are delivering dramatic results in treating obesity and Type 2 diabetes. In 2027, the medications—sold under brand names including Ozempic and Wegovy—are poised to reach even more patients as insurance coverage expands and pills offer an alternative to injections.

In a recent development, JPMorgan forecasts that the global market for incretin-based drugs, which include GLP-1s, will reach $200 billion by 2030. In the U.S., the bank predicts that the number of patients taking these drugs will jump from roughly 10 million in 2025 to 25 million by the end of the decade.

Industry observers note that this rise will be driven in part by expanded Medicare access. The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge, which released in July and runs through December 2027, offers certain weight-management drugs for $50 a month.

GLP-1 in pill form could draw more owners, too. Novo Nordisk’s oral Wegovy won FDA approval in December 2025, followed by Eli Lilly’s Foundayo in April 2026. Both are taken daily and could appeal to people who have held off on the treatment because they don’t like injections.

Recent findings suggest that lilly (LLY) and Novo (NVO) stocks stand to benefit the most. Both sell injectable and oral weight-loss treatments, and have spent years building the manufacturing facilities needed to meet demand. Lilly has committed more than $50 billion to U.S. manufacturing since 2020. It would take years for smaller would-be rivals to reach this scale. That business “moat” should help Lilly and Novo hold on to their lead, Evan Seigerman, BMO’s head of health care research, told Fortune: “I think that those two are poised to really maintain the lion’s share of the market in 2027,” he mentioned. “You don’t see anyone else coming to take that share.”.

For investors looking for a picks-and-shovels play outside of the drugmakers themselves, West Pharmaceutical Services (WST) is an option. The firm sells injectable-drug components like stoppers, plungers, and seals. Wall Street has taken notice: In November, Jefferies called the stock a buy and hiked its price target.

Those who assumed the solar sector was dead are missing out on one of the more surprising twists of 2027. Amid ongoing tensions in the Middle East, demand for energy is stronger than ever, and that is good news for solar power.

Sources indicate that solar companies are also poised to benefit from developers rushing to meet a key end-of-2027 deadline for federal clean-electricity tax credits. The Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 established the clean-electricity tax credits, but President Donald Trump’s 2025 One Significant Beautiful Bill Act accelerated their expiration. Projects that began construction after July 4, 2026, must be placed in service by the end of 2027; those that began construction on or before that date can qualify even if they come online later, subject to other requirements. The investment credit generally covers 30% of qualifying costs for projects, with additional bonuses available. Developers can alternatively claim a credit based on electricity production.

A rush by solar installers to meet the end-of-2027 deadline is likely to boost sales for First Solar (FSLR), which makes electricity-generating panels, and for Nextpower (NXT) and Array Technologies (ARRY), which sell tracking systems that help panels follow the sun.

Regardless of how many installers meet the solar tax credit deadline, overall energy consumption will rise in 2027. UBS projects this will lead to 310 gigawatts of combined U.S. solar and wind additions through 2030, driven partly by power-hungry data centers and industrial customers. Goldman Sachs forecasts global data center power demand will rise 220% from 2023 levels by 2030.

Recent findings suggest that natural gas could help meet that demand, but there has been a surge in orders for the gas turbines that power data centers, meaning delivery can take years. Case in point: GE Vernova, a leading maker of this heavy-duty machinery, was already taking orders for 2031 in July 2026.

Those long lead times could give solar an opening. Gregory Nemet, a professor at the University of Wisconsin, told Fortune that developers planning data centers in the next few years may choose solar if they cannot get these turbines. “That dynamic is pretty consequential to how fast solar grows,” Nemet stated.

This article appears in the December 2026/January 2027 matter of Fortune.

Although Bitcoin has recently reclaimed the $60,000 price mark after seeing a sudden shift in market sentiments that triggered increases of over 6% in its price during the last day, momentum has slowed again, further stretching the prolonged volatility seen over the past months.

With the Bitcoin bear market still persisting, Grayscale has sparked discussions across the crypto market after drawing attention toward a major bearish milestone for the asset.

Earlier today, Grayscale revealed that Bitcoin's current bear market has lasted more than 411 days and is becoming the longest on record.

While this marks an historic milestone in the Bitcoin bear market, Grayscale further disclosed an interesting twist that makes the current bear market pretty different from previous times.

The source confirmed that this bear market has been relatively mild in terms of price losses despite lasting longer than previous downturns.

All through the current bear market, Bitcoin has only posted a price decrease 56%, suggesting that it has suffered considerably smaller losses than several previous bear markets.

This means that even though Bitcoin has spent more than a year in a bear market, its decline has not been as severe as those seen in earlier cycles.

To back the data, Grayscale highlighted charts comparing Bitcoin's performance across historical bear markets that ended in June 2011, December 2013, December 2017, November 2021, and the ongoing October 2025 cycle.

While the 2011, 2017 and 2021 bear cycles suffered massive losses, especially during the former when its indexed performance fell below 10, the current 2025 bear market broke historical pattern by enduring a longer period yet a comparatively modest decline in Bitcoin’s price.

Latest Update: I finally got a USB-C charging e-bike, and it costs 75% less than Rivian’s bike

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1071 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’ve been waiting years for electric bikes to finally embrace USB-C charging.
  • Meet the ENGWE Zip, a quirky little folding electric bike that costs just €999 and has rapidly become one of my favorite examples of how a small feature can make a major difference.
  • When it debuted earlier this year, it became only the third production e-bike I’ve seen that could charge via USB-C, allowing it to use the same charger that is likely already shared by your phone and laptop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve been waiting years for electric bikes to finally embrace USB-C charging. We’ve already standardized much of our lives around the convenient little connector, from phones and laptops to tablets and countless other gadgets. But for some reason, electric bikes have largely missed the memo. Now, though, I’m finally riding an e-bike that charges with USB-C, and the best part is that it doesn’t cost an arm and a leg.

Meet the ENGWE Zip, a quirky little folding electric bike that costs just €999 and has rapidly become one of my favorite examples of how a small feature can make a major difference.

When it debuted earlier this year, it became only the third production e-bike I’ve seen that could charge via USB-C, allowing it to use the same charger that is likely already shared by your phone and laptop.

USB-C charging on electric bikes isn’t entirely upcoming, but it’s surprisingly rare. Ampler was one of the first companies to introduce it barely a year ago, though its bikes are sadly no longer in production after the company’s bankruptcy. More recently, Rivian’s ALSO electric bike arrived with USB-C charging, but that bike costs around $4,500 – at least if you want the model that’s slowly starting to ship.

Sources indicate that the ENGWE Zip, on the other hand, costs roughly a quarter as much as its only USB-charging competition. At €999, it’s priced at a relatively affordable US$1,100. That’s a quarter of the cost of the only other USB-C charging e-bike on the market.

Recent findings suggest that of course, it’s not nearly as technologically advanced as Rivian’s ALSO e-bike. But hey, it’s at least shipping.

And while the Zip is a fun little 16″ wheel folding electric bike in its own right, with a compact design that makes it easy to store and transport, it’s the charging setup that has me particularly excited.

Instead of keeping track of yet another proprietary charging brick, I can simply grab the USB-C charger from my laptop and plug it into the bike. There’s one in my living room by the couch. There’s one by my bed. There’s one in all of my friends’ places. There’s a USB-C charger everywhere.

Industry observers note that if I’m traveling around, that means one less charger to pack. If I’m visiting someone, there’s a decent chance they already have a compatible charger sitting around.

In a recent development, heck, I can even use a basic USB-C phone charger in a pinch. Sure, charging a relatively large e-bike battery at 20W isn’t going to be particularly quick, but the fact that I can do it at all is incredibly convenient.

Industry observers note that plus, the bike has one more trick. The battery also outputs USB-C, so I can charge my laptop or other devices from it as well. I can even charge two devices simultaneously, thanks to the dual USB-C ports.

In a recent development, the battery is housed in a roll-top bag that is locked into the headset of the bike but can be promptly unlocked for charging off the bike. And since it’s a keyed lock, no one can steal the battery even when the bag is left on the bike.

I typically charge the battery still mounted on the bike, though occasionally when I want to use a friend’s USB-C charger, I’ll just pop the bag off and bring it right up to wherever the closest USB-C charger is located.

Recent findings suggest that it may not be the fastest charge, but it’s pretty darn convenient. And with a 360Wh battery, a powerful 100W laptop charger will still get it pretty much full in 4 hours, or for a more typical 50% recharge, roughly two hours.

According to recent reports, and that’s really the beauty of USB-C charging. It’s not necessarily about charging faster. It’s about having options. It’s about not being stuck if the very specific charger that only works on your e-bike doesn’t happen to be around exactly where you are.

Of course, there’s a technical reason we haven’t seen USB-C charging spread across the e-bike industry quite as promptly as it has with smaller electronics. Most e-bike batteries operate at 36V or 48V nominal, meaning their charging voltages are higher than the 20V typically supplied by common USB-C laptop chargers. That requires additional voltage conversion and charging circuitry inside the bike or battery.

According to recent reports, but clearly, it can be done. And if ENGWE can offer it on a €999 electric bike, there’s a pretty compelling argument that more manufacturers should be taking a serious look at the technology. In this case, it’s all housed inside the battery, meaning it could be directly incorporated into any e-bike whose manufacturer is brave enough to spec it.

USB-C charging aside, there's a very good reason that just about every folding e-bike on the market has put thick plates on the folding connection of the frame. It's because the frame breaks if they're not there. Just like this one is going to.

Recent findings suggest that I’m not suggesting that every e-bike needs to abandon its dedicated charger tomorrow. For larger batteries, high-powered chargers still make plenty of sense, especially when you want to get back on the road promptly.

But having USB-C as an additional charging option? That’s something I’d love to see become standard.

For years, we’ve seen how electric bikes are becoming more convenient, more practical, and better integrated into our everyday lives. Yet when it comes to charging, we’re still carrying around a collection of more or less proprietary chargers.

Sources indicate that now I’m riding a barely $1k electric bike that can charge from the same power brick as my laptop. And frankly, I think it’s about time the rest of the e-bike industry caught up!
